resources.string: Allow MCP remote control (trips, sampling, capture)

The PC can end and start trips, change sampling, and take quick captures (finalizar_viaje, iniciar_viaje, set_muestreo, iniciar_captura, detener_captura). Use only on trusted networks: the token is sent unencrypted over Wi-Fi.
borrar_dtc requires the vehicle to be stopped and your tap on the notification, and resets readiness monitors: an inspection station may reject the vehicle until you complete drive cycles.

Clear codes by module (UDS 14), reset the ECU (UDS 11), run on-board tests (Mode 08), use manufacturer catalog operations, and send raw sequences. Each write requires your tap on a notification; writes never run while the vehicle is moving, and flashing is blocked.
These permissions are not included in backups: restoring a backup never enables them.
MCP writes run without asking you. Bypass turns off automatically when the MCP server stops.

Any client with the MCP token could clear codes, reset modules, and send manufacturer commands to the ECU without your approval. A wrong command can leave a module unusable until it is serviced by a dealer. The stopped-vehicle safeguards and flash blocking remain active.
Provider used to explain DTCs and local information. Without an API key, these features appear without AI explanations.

While driving with the dashboard open. Turning this off saves battery when using a car mount.
With the adapter connected and no active trip (after “End trip (stay connected)”), a trip starts when you maintain 10 km/h for 5 seconds.

Optional. Connect the app to a RevScope server to share spaces, go on group rides, and create ghost rides. The app works the same without it. Use the public server, one for your group, or host your own (github.com/santiquiroz/revscope-server). Leave this blank to use none.
Token (only if the server asks for one—leave blank otherwise)

When you arrive somewhere new, at home or abroad, it gives you a driving brief: fuel prices, tolls, restrictions, and what you need to drive there if you are outside your country. It checks the collaborative server first (free). If no one has reported that area and you have AI with web search, it generates a brief and shares it for the next traveler. Off by default (AI fallback costs money).
Notifies you when the brief is ready; details appear in the notification.
